claim: onlyfansstatistics.com reports OnlyFans median creator income of ~$180/year against a mean of $1,253/year, but explicitly attributes every percentile tier to unnamed 'third-party panel analyses' with no sample size, no panel name, no collection method and no date — the figure is untraceable.
stance_target: The claim that the widely-circulated OnlyFans median-earnings figure rests on a documented methodology
scope_conditions: OnlyFans platform only; page last updated 27 July 2026; no country stated — denominator is global registered accounts; tier figures self-described as 'estimates ... directional', sourced only to '[PANEL-2024] Third-party panel analyses for distribution percentiles (estimated)'
quoted_support: These figures are estimates derived from third-party data sources and should be treated as directional. Fenix International does not publish the underlying distribution; the company only reports the aggregate $5.80B payout figure.

claim: The only audited OnlyFans earnings figure is the $5.80B aggregate creator payout in Fenix International Ltd's FY2024 UK filing; the aggregator itself concedes that all per-creator distribution figures are unaudited estimates.
stance_target: The claim that platform-level aggregate payouts are verifiable but per-creator distributions on OnlyFans are not disclosed by the platform
scope_conditions: Fenix International Ltd FY2024 audited UK Companies House filing; aggregate payout only, no distributional breakdown; gross fan payments reported as $7.22B for FY2024 with payouts approximately 80% of that
quoted_support: Only one number here is audited. The $5.80B aggregate payout comes from Fenix International's FY2024 UK filing. Every percentile tier is a panel-derived estimate — useful and directionally consistent across sources, but not disclosure.

claim: The circulated OnlyFans mean of $1,253/creator/year is an arithmetic artifact of dividing total payouts by all registered accounts including dormant ones, and sits above the estimated top-25% earnings threshold (~$1,050/year) — meaning more than three-quarters of accounts never reach the 'average'.
stance_target: The claim that mean creator earnings are a structurally misleading statistic on power-law platforms and that survivorship/denominator choice drives headline numbers
scope_conditions: Denominator is 4.63M registered creator accounts including dormant and never-posted accounts; the site's own live counter shows 4.24M creators, an unexplained internal inconsistency; medians computed over active creators only would run 'far higher'
quoted_support: Dividing $5.80B in payouts by 4.63M creator accounts gives a $1,253/year mean — but that mean sits above the estimated top-25% threshold (~$1,050/year). On a power-law distribution, the "average" is an income that more than three-quarters of creators never reach.

claim: The OnlyFans payout-share tiers circulated in press — top 1% ~33%, top 10% ~73%, bottom 50% ~3% — appear on this page as estimates with no underlying study, and the bottom-50% share is stated as ~3%, not the ~1.5% cited elsewhere, showing the figures drift between aggregators.
stance_target: The claim that OnlyFans concentration percentages are stable, sourced statistics rather than drifting aggregator estimates
scope_conditions: OnlyFans only; estimated tiers: top 0.1% ~$735,000/yr and ~13% of payouts, top 1% ~$49,000/yr and ~33%, top 10% ~$5,200/yr and ~73%, top 25% ~$1,050/yr, median ~$180/yr, bottom 50% ~$50/yr and ~3%; no sample size or year given for the estimation panel

claim: The one directly measured concentration figure on the page — a scrape of 100,200 public OnlyFans profiles in June 2026 — shows attention is more concentrated than the income estimates claim: the top 10% of creators hold 82% of all likes and the bottom 50% hold roughly 0.2%.
stance_target: The claim that creator-economy attention and earnings follow extreme winner-take-most concentration, and that estimated income curves may understate it
scope_conditions: n=100,200 public creator profiles, June 2026, collected by onlyfansstatistics.com with sister site bestonlyfansreviews.com; likes are cumulative lifetime counts not dollars; directory-listed profiles skew toward active discoverable creators, not the full 4.63M registered accounts — a survivorship bias the source itself flags; no country breakdown
quoted_support: at every point where the two curves can be compared, measured attention is more concentrated than the earnings-tier estimates suggest. The top 10% of creators hold 82% of all likes versus an estimated ~73% of payouts; the bottom 50% hold roughly 0.2% of likes versus an estimated ~3% of payouts.

claim: No income Gini coefficient (the widely-cited 0.85 for OnlyFans) and no '70% of creators earn less than $100 monthly' survey figure appear anywhere on the leading OnlyFans statistics aggregator, despite the page being a dedicated income-distribution report.
stance_target: The claim that the OnlyFans 0.85 Gini and the '70% earn under $100/month' 2022 survey figure have a traceable published source
scope_conditions: Audited absence: the page is a dedicated OnlyFans income-distribution report published 2026 listing four sources ([FENIX-2024], [PANEL-2024], [OFS-DATASET-2026], [FORBES-2024]) and none is a survey of creators; neither the Gini nor the $100/month figure is present
quoted_support: Sources: [FENIX-2024] Fenix International Ltd — FY2024 audited filing for total payouts. [PANEL-2024] Third-party panel analyses for distribution percentiles (estimated). [OFS-DATASET-2026] onlyfansstatistics.com × bestonlyfansreviews.com creator dataset — 100,200 public profiles, June 2026

claim: Celebrity OnlyFans earnings figures circulated in press (Blac Chyna $20M/month, Bella Thorne $11M first week, Cardi B $9.5M/month) are self-reported peak-month spikes followed by 70-90% decay over six months, and are explicitly not audited.
stance_target: The claim that headline creator-income figures in press coverage are unaudited self-reports of peak periods, not sustained earnings
scope_conditions: Celebrity creators only, not representative of the creator population; figures from creator interviews, estate filings and platform-leaked rankings; decay estimate given without supporting data
quoted_support: These are peak-month figures, not sustained averages. Most celebrity OnlyFans launches see a sharp first-month spike followed by 70–90% decay over the following six months as initial subscriber rushes lapse.

claim: OnlyFans' nominal 80/20 creator-favorable split reduces to an estimated 65-72% real take-home for US-resident creators and 55-62% for international creators once payment processing, currency conversion and tax are deducted — but these ranges are given with no source.
stance_target: The claim that headline platform revenue splits overstate creator take-home income
scope_conditions: Estimates offered without citation; processing fees stated as 2.9% + ~$0.30 per transaction, currency conversion 1-3% spread; international figure assumes VAT obligations
quoted_support: Real take-home for a US-resident creator typically lands at 65–72% of the original fan payment. International creators with VAT obligations and FX spreads can land closer to 55–62%.
